title: Spelling Teams: oo
goal: I can spell words with oo, like moon and book.

card.desc: Bristol learns that the oo team says two sounds: the moon sound (moon, food, spoon, school, zoo) and the book sound (book, look, good, foot, cook, wood). Both are spelled with two o's. She sorts oo words by sound with word cards and fixes her spelling of bock for book.

win: Wow! The oo team is on your side too!

teacher.objective: Bristol learns that the oo team says two sounds, the moon sound (moon, food, spoon, school, zoo) and the book sound (book, look, good, foot, cook, wood), and that both are spelled with two o's. She sorts oo words by sound, tells oo from a short o (hot, dog, box), and fixes her bock-for-book spelling. Week 7 Day 2 (Practice it).
materials: The Class lesson open on your laptop (course page, code 9110)
10 index cards: moon, food, pool, zoo, tooth, book, look, foot, wood, cook
A small mirror (optional, for round lips on the moon sound)
Printed packet (2 pages) to send home

plan.do: Class slide 1. What does the ea team say?
Class slide 2. An ea word and an oo word from her book.
Class slide 3. Check Monday's After-Class score first.
Class slide 4. The moon sound and the book sound.
Class slides 5–6. She reads and spells each word.
Class slide 7. She reads each word out loud before she taps.
Class slide 8. She writes bock, crosses it out, writes book.
Class slide 9. Short o (hot, pot) vs. the oo team.
Class slide 10. Two piles, act out a word, a silly sentence.
Class slide 11. She reads every choice before she picks.
Class slides 12–13. Whiteboard first, then typed.
Class slide 14. She reads and underlines the oo words.
Class slide 16. Show the task list: tonight and Wednesday are the big homework days.

watch: bock for book (her own mistake), lok for look, mon for moon: one o. Ask: "Moon sound or book sound? Then it needs two o's."
u for the oo sounds (fud, gud, skool, spune). Say: "This week, that sound is spelled oo."
school spelled skool or scool. It is a word to remember: s-c-h-o-o-l.
Sorting by looks instead of sound. Have her say each word next to moon and next to book.
Some words sound different in different places (roof, room, root, broom). We do not sort these by sound in this lesson. If she says a word another way, accept her way.
Words like door and floor if she finds them. Say: "That is a different sound. We learn it later."

packet_key.answer: Any 2 oo words from her book, spelled right, each marked moon or book correctly.

slides.title: Meet the oo team
slides.text: oo is a vowel team too. It can say two sounds.

steps.text: 🌙 The moon sound. Say moon. Your lips make a small, round circle: ooo.
